title: Chief of Staff - Tactical digest and action track (pre-exec staff)
content:
Purpose: quick-read scratchpad for the exec staff meeting (Mon 2026-03-09). Single-page prep: flags, top asks by leader, open blockers, and the action tracker I will read out. Not final; meant to be terse so we can hit decisions in the 40m slot.

Context / framing:
- Recent incidents raised two themes: capacity fragility at 512-token streams and rollout risk for the new batching engine. Teams have short-term mitigations but need exec alignment on prioritization vs Dedicated capacity commits.
- GTM wants firm language on Dedicated SLAs for 2 strategic customers by EOW; product/infra need contract runway.

Agenda bullets (read out in ~3 mins):
1) Quick incident recap + mitigation ask (Marco) — decision: pause non-critical model variants for 24h?
2) Dedicated capacity commercial ask (Nina) — decision: approve customer-specific SLA template + runway
3) Rollout plan for batching engine (Marco + SRE) — decision: canary cadence and rollback triggers
4) Cross-org hiring prioritization (People) — ratify two senior infra roles or defer to next hiring cycle
5) AOB: legal note on new KMS audit language (Sasha)

Top asks (one-liners by leader):
- Marco (Eng): Need green light to throttle low-priority background inference to protect tail latency for served traffic. Risk: slight revenue impact for background jobs.
- Nina (Product): Approve contract clause A.3 (guaranteed regional residency) for two pilot customers; we need legal sign-off to go to PoC.
- Liam (SRE): Approve extending emergency burn credits to North region for two weeks while we add nodes.
- Sasha (Security): Sign-off on the updated KMS audit wording; minimal change to TOS but needs exec concurrence.

Open blockers (short):
- Capacity forecasting: finance and infra numbers mismatch by ~15% for Q2 committed GPU hours. Action: ops->Finance sync by Wed (Evan).
- Canary metrics: no agreed SLI for degraded quality vs cost-savings in quantized models. Action: product/metrics draft by Fri (Nina).
- Legal turnaround: SLA template needs redlines; legal asks 3 business days. If we want to hit GTM date, need exec approval to accept legal minimal redlines.

Action tracker (to read; format: action — owner — due — status):
- Provide short risk memo on halting non-critical variants — Marco — 2026-03-09 09:00 — in progress
- Draft customer-specific SLA + attachment for residency — Nina — 2026-03-10 17:00 — in progress
- Add two temporary nodes to north cluster and validate perf — SRE ops team / Liam — 2026-03-12 — planned
- Inventory of last week's incident impact (who, which customers, token loss) — support ops / Akiko — 2026-03-11 — in progress
- Legal redline summary (one bullet per change) — Legal / Sasha — 2026-03-10 — requested

1:1 focused notes (upcoming):
- CEO (30m): focus on GTM ask and whether to pre-approve SLA language. Ask: if we push SLA, what tradeoffs are acceptable? My prep: show worst-case unit economics for the pilot (slide 3).
- Marco (20m): tactical unblock for canary triggers; ask for a decision on whether to pause low-priority variants. Bring: short metro chart of tail latencies, cost delta.
- Nina (20m): discuss product boundary for regional residency; align on minimal scope.

Decision scaffolding (options + recommended):
- Pause non-critical variants for 24h: Pros = immediate tail relief; Cons = revenue loss for background jobs. Recommendation: approve pause for 24h with clear customer comms for affected users.
- Approve SLA template now vs wait for legal: Pros = GTM momentum; Cons = risk of missing legal nuance. Recommendation: approve provisional exec sign-off with legal to finalize redlines in 72h.

Communication plan (if decisions made):
- Engineering will publish incident postmortem summary and list of affected variants to #prod-incidents within 2 hours after meeting.
- Sales/GTM draft: email to pilot customers with timeframe and mitigation language. Owner: Nina.

Done / actually-completed since last exec (micro wins):
- SRE shipped two autoscaler fixes that removed a noisy CPU spike (deployed 2026-03-02).
- Finance approved temporary overage buffer for March to prevent throttles during capacity migration.
- Small-batch model quantization test passed perf gate on internal dataset (Marco).

Open questions I want flagged to execs (fast):
- Do we want to formally prioritize low-latency SLAs over lower-cost background workloads for the next 2 quarters? (Yes/No)
- If we accept provisional SLA approval, who signs customer-facing SLA if legal final redlines come back after the PoC starts?

Notes to self (pre-meeting checklist):
- Upload slide 2 (risk matrix) to the meeting deck by EOD Fri.
- Ping legal + attach redline template in chat.
- Prep two-sentence readout for each agenda item for an easy handoff.
- Print final action tracker and share in meeting thread.

Backburner / parking lot (do not read unless called):
- Longer-term: run workload-specific quantization trials that preserve eval quality at tail lengths >512.
- Ops: billing mapping for Dedicated reserved hours per team; upstream proposal due Q3.

If anything changes before meeting: I will update this doc and push to the meeting thread; otherwise, assume the above is the live pre-read.

Quick contact map:
- Marco Li (eng lead): marco@redwood.ai (Slack: @marco)
- Nina Patel (product lead): nina@redwood.ai (Slack: @nina)
summary: One-page tactical pre-read for exec staff: incidents, asks, decisions, and an action tracker to read aloud. Focused on capacity fragility, Dedicated SLA ask, batching engine rollout, and quick 1:1 prep notes.
